entities.summary: Fulgentius Ferrandus or Ferrand of Carthage was a Christian theologian of the Roman province of Africa, modern day Tunisia, known for his influential writings on the Trinity and the nature of God. Born in the 5th century CE, Ferrand was educated in Greek and Latin, and traveled to Rome and Constantinople to engage in theological debates. His most famous work, the De Trinitate, was a defense of the divinity of Christ and the Holy Spirit, and had a significant impact on the development of Trinitarian theology in the Western Church. Ferrand was also a prolific writer on other theological topics, including the nature of the soul and the sacraments. His writings were widely read and respected in his lifetime, and he was considered one of the leading theologians of his era. Despite his significant contributions to Christian theology, Ferrand's life and work are not well-documented, and much of what is known about him comes from later sources. Nevertheless, his legacy as a theologian and scholar continues to be felt today.
